annotations.text:
THE BAR THIS IS DRAWN TO

The reference is Fungies and Tiny Tower: characters you tell apart at a glance, three tones and a hard outline, no realism.

Measured against our own canvas, that bar is comfortably reachable. At the graphics rung a worker gets about 142x192 real pixels; a Tiny Tower bitizen is roughly 32x48. We have four times the room.

What was missing was never resolution. It was that the art had never been redrawn to use it.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED

Before: a worker was two eye pixels on a coloured rectangle, about 16 units tall, with no arms.

Now: 24 x 34 units carrying brows, eyes, nose, mouth, framed hair, a torso with arms that end in hands, legs and shoes. Six wardrobe slots still assemble it from parts.

The floor board is the same room with those people in it, drawn at 4x. Nothing about the room changed except that you can now see who is in it.

WHAT THIS CANVAS IS AND IS NOT

These are proposals rendered from real pixel maps, not mockups painted by hand - the same maps can be ported straight into the renderer.

They are not final art. Faces have one expression, there is no walk cycle here, and the props each worker holds are specified but not drawn.

The guard office and the settings screen are not covered at all.

THE ONE DECISION THAT GATES EVERYTHING

This quality needs the graphics rung. At sextants a worker is 35x36 and carries silhouette, shirt and hair but not a face; at half-blocks it is 17x24 and carries almost nothing.

So either the graphics path becomes the product and characters degrade deliberately below it, or the design targets 35x36 and stays much simpler than the reference.

Everything on these boards assumes the first. That is the choice to confirm before anyone builds.
